claim_scope: RSC Advances 2015 review states MoS2 has three known polytypes - 1T, 2H, and 3R - distinguished by the coordination of Mo and by layer stacking (2H and 3R: trigonal-prismatic; 1T: octahedral). Secondary-scholarly framework establishing the polytype distinction. Section 2.1 of the publisher-hosted article also explicitly explains the polytype naming convention: the numeral is the count of S–Mo–S layers per crystallographic unit cell and T/H/R indicate trigonal/hexagonal/rhombohedral structure; this is a secondary descriptive convention, not an additional primary determination.

polytype_label_convention.numeral: number of S–Mo–S layers within a crystallographic unit cell
polytype_label_convention.origin: Song, Park and Choi (2015), section 2.1, published review

locator.verbatim: three known polytypes - namely 1T, 2H, and 3R - of MoS2 ... 2H and 3R commonly have trigonal prismatic coordination (D3h) of molybdenum atoms, but they have different stacking order.
